title: The pull request
note: 84% dead picture across eight spans - the frame is a static pull request page while the narration teaches how to read one. Six cutaways, 67s of 156s (43%). The two sync leads (anchors 38.1 and 103.4) are 4s and 5s, under the 8s threshold, and neither has a dead frame in the three seconds before it to end a card on.

inserts.why: Names the lecture and the argument it closes. The four parts of the PR are spoken in the first seven seconds and sit in the title card's stamp.

slides.stamp: a title, a body, a branch, and a link back to the issue it closes

inserts.why: The body of the pull request is on the frame and unreadable at 4K, and the narration is reading it out. This is that body at a size you can read, then the reason the third heading is the one that matters. The editor card held for nine seconds and 15-32 read as dead picture, so the focus now moves from the first heading to the third instead of sitting on it.

slides.kicker: the body it wrote, at a size you can read

rows.t: ## What changed
The parser trimmed the trailing field, so a row
ending in a comma lost its last value.
## Why
The split ran before the guard, not after it.
## What I deliberately did not do
Did not rename the function, did not tidy the
imports, did not touch the second parser.
